The hour or so of awake time was used for quiet reflection, sex, smoking and pretty much everything except staring at the wall terrified of insomnia. The normal sleep pattern is to sleep shortly after the sun goes down. Wake again around midnight to two. Go back to sleep at roughly three to six. And then up again around eight to eleven. It's believe this schedule exists because of the need for cooperative lookouts against night time predators. If we look back at many old books, they speak of nocturnal activities based on these odd-ball schedules; which I believe is the origin of "burning the midnight oil."

As modern society began to evolve we started interfering with natural sleep cycles. This includes paying people to rouse us at specific times. Which eventually led to alarm clocks and more rigid social schedules.

As for my current situation. I sleep whenever I feel like to and actually try to find the best sleep length.

Got myself an Apple Watch. I loaded an App called heartwatch (there are plenty of other apps that do the same, I'm not trying to shill this app.) I told the app I need 7 hours of sleep. I switch it to sleep mode and lie down. Here's what I learned, I wake several times during the night. It doesn't matter. If I spend 8.5 hours tossing and turning trying to sleep, I feel good. That was a surprise to me. I also slept rock solid for 7 hours but woke and felt tired. I've woken at 7 hours and forced myself to lay there for one more hour and woke up an hour and a half later, fully rested. The bottom line is I felt more rested tossing and turning for 8 and half hours than sleeping solid for seven hours. Crazy stuff.
